counting.sequence.recite.root_reason: The number words one through nineteen are memorized as a rote sequence; a child needs no earlier skill in this map to say them in order.

edges.why: Counting backward reverses the memorized forward order of number words, so the learner must already hold that order to run it in reverse.

counting.one-to-one.root_reason: The assessment credits tagging each object exactly once with any number words, whether or not they are in conventional order, so neither the word sequence nor any quantity idea is required.

cardinality.small-number-words.root_reason: This is the first mapping of the words one, two and three to exact quantities, learned from experience with small sets before counting is used to find how many.

edges.why: A collection counted correctly requires the number words said in their conventional order, and the last of those words is what names the total.

A numeral stands for how many objects are in a set, so pairing it with a set requires finding how many by counting the set.
Writing the numeral for a spoken number uses the learned link between each digit symbol and its number word, the same link used in reading.
Making exactly one mark for each car keeps every object paired once and none skipped or doubled, the same tagging discipline as one word per object.

Naming a briefly shown set means applying a number word that already names an exact quantity, extended here from one to three up through four or five.

subitizing.nonverbal.root_reason: Making a matching set after a glimpse uses direct perception of small exact quantity and requires no number words, so nothing earlier in the map is needed.

edges.why: Each part of the arrangement, such as the five and the two, must itself be named at a glance, which is the perceptual skill.
Knowing the whole the recognized parts make means finding the total of two sets joined together, the meaning of joining and counting all.

comparing.count.perceptual.root_reason: Telling which of two very unequal sets has more uses direct perception of large quantity differences, with no counting or other earlier skill in this map.

edges.why: Judging that three cars and three buttons are the same number requires apprehending each small set's exact quantity directly without words, even when the objects differ.

comparing.count.matching.root_reason: Pairing each object in one collection with an object in the other uses no number words or counting, so a child can do it with nothing earlier in the map.

edges.why: Steps one and two count each collection to get its number, and the test problem counts six buttons and four blocks.

shapes.match.root_reason: Picking the shape that is the same as a given shape, despite size or orientation, rests on visual perception of form and needs no earlier skill in this map.

shapes.name.prototype.root_reason: Learning the words circle, square and triangle for typical examples is a label association made from experience with those shapes, with no earlier skill in this map required.

edges.why: The test asks for all triangles, so the learner must have the shape class names, learned first for typical examples.

Rejecting a triangle with a curved side or an open three-sided figure requires attending to whether the sides are straight segments forming a closed boundary.
The sides are pointed to one at a time and counted, so the learner counts a set of segments by tagging each once and giving the last word.
A corner is defined as a point where two sides meet, so the learner must already identify the sides of the shape.
The corners are touched one at a time and counted, so the learner counts a set of points with each tagged once.
Deciding two shapes are the same extends picking a shape that is the same as a given one, here requiring exact sameness of size and every part.

Choosing a turn, slide or flip to make a triangle fit requires seeing that the turned piece is the same shape as the outline.

spatial.position.body.root_reason: Direction words for one's own body are learned from direct movement and spoken instruction, with no earlier skill in this map required.

spatial.position.relative.root_reason: Position words such as in, on, under and behind are learned from direct experience with objects in space, so no earlier skill in this map is required.

classifying.alike.root_reason: Seeing two objects as alike or different is a basic perceptual judgment that needs no earlier skill in this map.

edges.why: Naming the attribute a group shares starts from seeing that the objects are alike, then saying in what way.
Sorting by a stated attribute such as color requires treating color as one attribute with separate values and ignoring the other attributes like size.
